classification.difficultyReason: Transfer the given edge weights into a supplied adjacency table and explain symmetry using the taught undirected-edge relationship.

inlines.text: Represent this graph using a table.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 1, graph to the left of the blank adjacency table
spec.description: Undirected complete network on four vertices; W above, Y lower left, X lower right and Z inside the triangle. Ordinary source blue vertices and labels use house black.
spec.mathematics: WX=10, WY=12, WZ=6, XY=11, XZ=6, YZ=8. Six edges; no arrows or loops.
spec.answerVisibility: All vertices, edges and weights are permanent student-visible givens.

inlines.text: Enter each edge weight in both matching cells because the graph is undirected. There are no loops, so mark each diagonal cell with a dash. With columns W, X, Y, Z, the completed rows are:

children.label: b
children.prompt: Explain why the table is symmetrical along the diagonal.

answer.short: The graph is undirected, so each edge has the same weight in both directions.
answer.worked: Each edge can be travelled in either direction with the same weight. For example, W to X and X to W both have weight 10. Each pair of cells reflected across the diagonal therefore has the same entry.
